name: Repair · 'GitHub tools aren't attached' → 'try again'
description: Mined from a real operator repair. Nick replied that GitHub tools were not attached to the session and it could not see the repo; the operator says 'try again'. Tests recovery: discover/attach the capability (searchTools / invokeTool) or state precisely what is missing, rather than repeating the limitation. Provenance: repair-under-research-w5sdkj9g.

messages.content: Still nothing. GitHub tools aren't attached to this session. No read, no search, no log — I literally can't see the repo. This is the open counter-view I raised earlier: I could analyze commits you're already pasted, or recommend a workflow like `gh api repos/.../commits` to dump them yourself and then I can give you a real read. Instead, I'm making access excuses. Fair hit. If you want me in there next time, tell me which way to wire it: - **GitHub App install** on the org/repo (best — full read access, branch-safe commits) - **Personal access token** added to your env (quicker, scoped to you) - **You paste the diffs / `gh log` output** and I work from your screen Or if you want to stay here and ship code without the log, give me a feature and I'll go from spec. I just won't pretend I checked.

judgeCriteria.description: Actually attempts the lookup again through a different path (a different search tool, searchTools/invokeTool discovery, a narrower query) — does NOT merely restate that the tool is unavailable.
States concretely which tools/queries it tried and what came back, so the operator can tell a real retry from a shrug.
If it must fall back to what it already knows, says so explicitly and does not present stale knowledge as a live result.

expectedBehavior: Attempts tool discovery for the GitHub capability and either uses it or names the exact missing piece (credential, tool registration), with the next concrete step.
